questions.stem: A vertical cylindrical pipe is cut by four section planes: P-P is a vertical plane parallel to the axis; Q-Q is a horizontal plane perpendicular to the axis; R-R and S-S are planes inclined to the axis. Which of the cut sections of the cylindrical pipe will show a rectangle as its true shape?
questions.explanation: A plane parallel to the axis of a cylinder cuts it along straight generators, giving a rectangular section; a perpendicular plane gives a circle and an inclined plane an ellipse.

questions.stem: If the exterior angle of a regular polygon is 72°, the polygon is
questions.explanation: Number of sides = 360°/72° = 5, so the polygon is a pentagon.

questions.stem: In which of the following is the principle of the archimedean spiral employed in its construction?
options: Hair spring of a wrist watch.
questions.explanation: The coiled hair spring of a watch winds outward at a constant rate like an archimedean spiral; a screw thread follows a helix and a head lamp reflector is a parabola.

questions.stem: Which of the following angles can be trisected using a pair of compasses?
questions.explanation: One third of 90° is 30°, which can be constructed with compasses (bisecting a 60° angle); 20°, 40° and 50° cannot be constructed with compasses alone.

questions.stem: In a helix, the length of one complete turn is called the
questions.explanation: The pitch of a helix is the axial distance advanced in one complete revolution.

questions.stem: The similarity between a deltoid and a rhombus is that
options: their angles are all right angles.
their diagonals bisect at right angle.
questions.explanation: In both a deltoid (kite) and a rhombus the diagonals cross at right angles, one bisecting the other; a deltoid is not a parallelogram and its sides are not all equal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not required in the construction of a parabola?
questions.explanation: A parabola is constructed from its focus, directrix and vertex; a minor axis belongs to the ellipse.

questions.stem: To draw an escribed circle of a given triangle, the first step is to
questions.explanation: An escribed circle lies outside the triangle touching one side and the other two sides produced, so the sides are first extended before the exterior angles are bisected.

questions.stem: Two equal circles with centres O1 and O2 intersect at points A and B. In respect to the two circles, line AB is a
questions.explanation: AB joins two points on each circle without passing through either centre, so it is a (common) chord.

questions.stem: Which of the following workshop tools is used for finding the diameter of a round bar?
questions.explanation: A micrometer measures the diameter of a round bar accurately; an odd leg caliper is used for scribing lines parallel to an edge or finding centres.

questions.stem: A site plan shows the
questions.explanation: A site plan shows the position of buildings on the plot in relation to boundaries, roads and other features.

questions.stem: In which of the following types of floor construction is a wall plate used?
questions.explanation: In a hollow (suspended) timber ground floor the joists rest on timber wall plates bedded on sleeper walls.

questions.stem: The expression M12 x 2.5mm on the thread refers to
questions.explanation: In metric thread notation M12 x 2.5 means a nominal (major) diameter of 12 mm and a pitch of 2.5 mm.

questions.stem: A key shaped like a segment of a circular disc (flat top, semicircular bottom), which sits in a curved keyseat in the shaft, is called
questions.explanation: A woodruff key is a semicircular (disc-segment) key fitted into a matching curved keyseat.

questions.stem:
The following are all locking devices.
I. Split pin.
II. Spring washer.
III. Grub screw.
IV. Tab washer.
Which of them are frictional?
questions.explanation: A spring washer and a grub screw lock by friction and pressure; a split pin and a tab washer are positive locking devices.

questions.stem: How many faces has a solid hexagonal pyramid?
questions.explanation: Six triangular side faces plus one hexagonal base = 7 faces.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a type of orthographic projection?
questions.explanation: Isometric is a pictorial projection; first angle, third angle and auxiliary views are orthographic.

questions.stem: Three isometric axes OP, OQ and OR are drawn from a point O: OQ is vertical, while OP and OR slope upwards to the left and right. What is the value of the angle θ between OR and the horizontal?
questions.explanation: In isometric drawing the receding axes are drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

questions.stem: Which of the following drawing instruments is used to reproduce shapes?
questions.explanation: A template has cut-out standard shapes (circles, ellipses, symbols) which are traced to reproduce them quickly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a frustum?
questions.explanation: A bucket is shaped like a cone with its top cut off parallel to the base, i.e. a frustum.

questions.stem: The development of a closed square prism will have
questions.explanation: A closed square prism has four rectangular sides and two square ends.

questions.stem: If a length of 1 metre on land is represented by 2 cm on a drawing, what is the ratio of the scale used?
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm is shown as 2 cm, so the scale is 2:100 = 1:50.

questions.stem: Which of the following has eight triangular faces?
questions.explanation: A regular octahedron has eight equilateral triangular faces.

questions.stem: A sphere is cut by a section plane S-S inclined to its centre lines. Which of the following is the true shape of the section S-S if the object is spherical?
questions.explanation: Every plane section of a sphere, in any direction, is a circle.

questions.stem: A conic section whose eccentricity is 4/3 is a/an
questions.explanation: Eccentricity greater than 1 gives a hyperbola (e = 1 parabola, e < 1 ellipse).

questions.stem: If a right cone is truncated by a cutting plane which is perpendicular to its axis, then the true shape of the cut surface is a/an
questions.explanation: A plane perpendicular to the axis of a right cone cuts it in a circle.

questions.stem: The point where a line penetrates a plane is called the
questions.explanation: The trace of a line is the point where it meets (pierces) a plane of projection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a type of scale?
questions.explanation: Plain, diagonal and chord scales are standard types; there is no 'parallel scale'.

questions.stem: The head lamp of a car is constructed by applying the principle of
questions.explanation: A parabolic reflector sends light from a bulb at its focus out as a parallel beam.

questions.stem: A line PQ is divided by drawing a line from P at an acute angle, stepping off eleven equal units along it, joining the eleventh point to Q and drawing lines parallel to it through the other points. The construction cannot be used to
options: determine the mid-point of line PQ.
divide line PQ into eleven equal parts.
construct a triangle whose sides are in ratio 3:5:3
construct a triangle whose perimeter is equal to line PQ.
questions.explanation: With eleven (an odd number of) divisions no division point falls at the middle of PQ; the divisions do give eleven equal parts, a 3:5:3 split (3+5+3 = 11) and hence a triangle of perimeter PQ.

questions.stem: In a section through a roof and wall, the timber member S is laid on top of the wall and the rafter rests on it. The part labelled S is called
questions.explanation: The wall plate is the timber bedded on top of a wall to receive the feet of the rafters and spread their load.

questions.stem: In a staircase, the level platform P between two flights of steps is the
questions.explanation: A landing is the flat platform at the end of a flight or between flights.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a type of door?
questions.explanation: Raft is a type of foundation, not a door; ledged and batten (battern) doors are door types.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a member of a roof?
questions.explanation: A jamb is the vertical side member of a door or window frame; queen post, purlin and wall plate are roof members.

questions.stem: In a staircase, the horizontal upper surface X of a step, on which the foot is placed, is identified as the
questions.explanation: The horizontal part of a step (the tread) gives the going; the riser is the vertical part.

questions.stem: Soffit is a member of a
questions.explanation: A soffit is the underside lining of a roof overhang at the eaves.

questions.stem: In a roof truss, the central vertical member Q running from the tie beam to the apex is called
questions.explanation: The king post is the central vertical post of a truss joining the tie beam to the apex.

questions.stem: The bevelled edge X at the end of a cylindrical shaft is
questions.explanation: A bevelled edge on the end of a shaft is a chamfer, which removes the sharp corner.

questions.stem: The profile of a screw thread is constructed using the principle of a/an
questions.explanation: A screw thread is generated as a helix around a cylinder.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a type of key?
questions.explanation: A dowel is a locating pin; feather, gib-head and woodruff are keys.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a type of positive locking washer?
questions.explanation: A tab washer is bent up against the nut and the component, locking it positively; spring and star washers lock by friction.
